---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CashBackedROA_RankProduct
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating profitability is priced correctly only when it is corroborated by cash generation; the joint state of high operating ROA AND low total accruals identifies durable, non-reversing profitability that the market under-extrapolates.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The multiplicative rank structure gives credit only to firms scoring well on both dimensions, so it is not a mere additive re-labeling of either single-theme anchor. Firms with high ROA but large positive accruals get a low product because their earnings quality is suspect, while cash-rich but unprofitable firms are also excluded.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ProfitCashGate
EXPRESSION: MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability predicts returns only in the regime where operating cash flow exceeds reported earnings (negative accruals); in the accrual-financed regime the same reported profitability carries no information about future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator switches profitability on/off based on accrual sign, a genuinely conditional rather than blended interaction, testing whether the profitability premium is concentrated in cash-validated firms. If the premium survives only in the gated subsample, accrual quality is the state variable governing profitability's persistence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ProfitPerAccrualReliance
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 3)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The economically relevant quantity is cash profitability earned per unit of accounting-accrual reliance: firms generating high cash returns with minimal accrual distortion (in either direction) have the most credible, least manipulable earnings stream.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The denominator uses absolute accruals so that both aggressive income-increasing and big-bath income-decreasing accounting are penalized as evidence of low reporting reliability, which a signed accrual measure cannot capture. Three-year smoothing suppresses one-off working-capital swings, and winsorization controls the small-denominator explosion inherent to ratio interactions.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualInflatedProfit
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Reported profitability that is simultaneously in the top of the accrual distribution reflects transitory accounting-driven earnings that mean-revert, so the joint high-ROA/high-accrual state should forecast poor future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This deliberately isolates the reversal side of the mechanism rather than the reward side, providing an independent test of the same economic story with the opposite sign. Because the accrual anomaly is strongest where earnings levels are high enough to attract extrapolative pricing, the product should be more negatively predictive than accruals alone.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: GrossProfitVsWorkingCapitalPressure
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross profitability is a clean top-line measure of business quality, but it is only credible when it is not being manufactured by expanding working capital; industry-adjusted gross profit combined with low working-capital accrual pressure identifies genuinely efficient franchises.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Using gross profit avoids contamination from the same accrual items that appear in the accrual leg, making the two channels economically independent inputs rather than mechanical mirror images. Industry ranking of gross profitability handles the large cross-industry dispersion in cost structure, while the balance-sheet accrual leg captures receivable/inventory-financed sales growth.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ProfitLevelVsAccrualDrift
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained profitability is durable when the accrual component of earnings is stable or shrinking over time; a multi-year upward drift in accruals signals that a firm's profit level is progressively being borrowed from future periods.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This converts accrual quality from a one-period level into a trajectory concept, so it distinguishes firms whose current profitability rests on an increasingly fragile accounting base from those whose profits are converting into cash at a stable or improving rate. Smoothing profitability over three years ensures the profitability leg reflects a persistent state rather than a single strong year.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE CashBackedROA_RankProduct---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Operating ROA minus accruals is essentially cash-based operating profitability (Ball-Gerakos-Linnainmaa-Nikolaev), so the rank product is a cosmetic re-encoding of a well-documented anomaly rather than a new interaction.

---CRITIQUE ProfitCashGate---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Zeroing out the accrual-financed half of the universe creates a large point mass at exactly 0 that sits above all loss-making but cash-validated firms, so the sort no longer tests the stated conditional hypothesis and the spread will be driven by an artifact of the masking convention rather than by regime-dependent profitability pricing.

---CRITIQUE ProfitPerAccrualReliance---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A signed numerator over an absolute-value denominator is non-monotonic in the intended quality dimension — firms with negative cash ROA and clean (small) accruals receive the most extreme negative scores while messy loss-makers score near zero — so the expression contradicts the hypothesis, and 1% winsorization does not fix the small-denominator instability.

---CRITIQUE AccrualInflatedProfit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Since RANK(NEG(x)) ≈ 1 − RANK(x), this signal is (up to the oiadp/ib substitution) the exact algebraic complement of CashBackedROA_RankProduct conditional on the profitability rank, so it is a redundant sign-flipped restatement of the same known profitability-times-accruals combination rather than an independent test.

---CRITIQUE GrossProfitVsWorkingCapitalPressure---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The combination of Novy-Marx gross profitability with the Sloan balance-sheet accrual is a defensible and cleanly constructed composite with industry adjustment, though both legs are individually published and the claim of economic independence is overstated because credit-financed revenue inflates gross profit directly.

---CRITIQUE ProfitLevelVsAccrualDrift---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Replacing the accrual level with a five-year accrual trajectory is a genuinely distinct construct that is not a relabeling of the accrual anomaly, and the sign and hypothesis are internally coherent — the main risks to monitor are coverage loss from the long history requirement and trend noise from mean-reverting accruals.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ProfitabilityXAccrualInstability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: What distinguishes durable from fragile profitability is not the level of accruals (which is already embedded in cash-based operating profitability) but the instability of the accrual wedge: profitable firms whose earnings-minus-cash gap swings widely year to year have low-reliability accounting and their profits are more likely to reverse.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Replacing the accrual level with a five-year second moment breaks the algebraic equivalence to cash-based operating profitability, since a firm can have persistently large but stable accruals (high reliability) or small but erratic ones (low reliability) and the two receive opposite treatment here. The interaction is genuine because accrual volatility alone mostly proxies for business risk, while conditional on high operating ROA it identifies profits whose accounting support is unreliable.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ProfitImprovementCashValidated
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: An improvement in operating profitability is informative about future returns only when it is not accompanied by a simultaneous increase in accruals; margin gains delivered through accrual build-up are transitory and revert within a year or two.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The weakest-link MIN of two cross-sectional ranks implements the conditional logic continuously — a firm scores high only if it improves on both dimensions — and therefore avoids the degenerate point mass at zero created by the earlier indicator mask. Because both legs are first differences, the signal is orthogonal by construction to the level-based cash-based-profitability anomaly and tests whether accrual quality validates the change in profitability.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CashPurityWeightedProfitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ABS(MA(SUB(ib, oancf), 3)))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among equally profitable firms, the share of profit that arrives as cash rather than as accrual accounting is the credibility discriminator; a bounded cash-purity share, interacted with the profitability level, isolates firms whose reported profits are genuinely realized.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The purity ratio is bounded in [-1, 1] and is monotone increasing in cash backing, so the earlier non-monotonicity (clean loss-makers receiving the most extreme scores) is eliminated, and the denominator can only approach zero when both cash flow and accruals vanish, which winsorization then handles. Three-year averaging of both components stabilizes the share, and multiplying by industry-ranked profitability makes the score a profitability measure weighted by earnings credibility rather than a standalone quality ratio.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: MarginGainFinancedByWorkingCapital
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross-margin expansion that is simultaneously financed by a build-up in receivables and inventory reflects channel stuffing, loosened credit terms, or unsold production rather than real pricing power, so such profitability gains predict negative future abnormal returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This uses income-statement margin dynamics against specific cash-flow-statement working-capital components rather than the total earnings-minus-cash wedge, so it is not the sign-flipped complement of any level-based profitability-times-accrual product. The COALESCE fallback to the balance-sheet change in non-cash current assets is economically equivalent in sign and preserves coverage for firms and periods where the cash-flow-statement detail lines are unreported.
